The PSI of Kamakshipalya police station has filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable u/s 498(A) of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act.
 2.
The case of the prosecution in nutshell is as follows :
The marriage of the complainant was took place along with the accused on 12.02.2018 at temple near Chennapattana and they have registered their marriage at SubRegister office.

After the marriage, the accused and complainant were residing at No.4, 9th Cross,
Hoysala Nagar, Sunkadakatte, Bangalore.
On  3 CC.16042/2022 03.08.2021 at about 10.00 pm the accused picked up quarrel with the complainant for no reason and abused her in filthy language by demanding to bring the additional dowry.
The accused assaulted the complainant violently with his hands, kicked him with his legs and gave physical and mental torture to her.
Due to this, on 04.08.2021 at about 8.45 am the complainant left the house of the accused and went to Maddur and took shelter in CW7's house.
Therefore, the complainant gave complaint against accused.

3. Based on the complaint given by the The State By Kamakshipalya vs Ajit on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141882436/
2 complainant, the FIR was registered against the accused for the offence punishable U/s 498(A) of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act.
After filing the charge sheet, this court has taken cognizance against the accused and summons was issued to accused, but he has not appeared before the.
In pursuance of the NBW the accused appeared before the court and enlarged on bail.
4. Thereafter the prosecution papers has been furnished to the accused as contemplated U/Sec 207 of  4 CC.16042/2022 Cr.P.C.
Thereafter heard the learned prosecution and counsel for accused about framing of charge.
Since there were sufficient materials to frame charge against the accused, charges were framed u/s 498(A) of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act.
The sum and substance of the accusation was read over to the accused and his answers to the said accusation was denial and he claimed to be tried.
Hence, the prosecution was given an opportunity to establish the guilt of the accused.
5. The prosecution in order to bring home the guilt of the accused, it got examined only one witness as PW1 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P.1 and Ex.P2.

Since PW1 being the complainant has turned hostile to the prosecution case, the prayer of the learned APP for examining the other witnesses have been rejected and remaining witnesses have been dropped as no purpose would be served.

Since there is The State By Kamakshipalya vs Ajit on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141882436/
3 no any incriminating evidence against the accused, the statement of the accused as required U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.

sentences.text:
6. Heard the arguments of learned prosecution and counsel for accused.
 7.

The points that arise for consideration of this Court are as under :
 :: POINTS ::
 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the marriage of the accused was took place along with the CW1 on 12.02.2018 at temple near Chennapattana and they got registered their marriage at SubRegister office.

After the marriage when the accused and CW1 were residing at No.4, 9th Cross, Hoysala Nagar, Sunkadakatte, Bangalore, on 03.08.2021 at about 10.00 pm the accused picked up quarrel with the CW1 for no reason and abused her in filthy language and the accused assaulted the complainant violently with his hands, kicked him with his legs and thereby given physical and mental cruelty to her and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 498A of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the same date, time,
the accused demanded to bring additional dowry and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
3. What Order?

8. The findings of this Court on above points are as under: Point No.1 & 2: In Negative Point No.3 :
As per the final order for the following: REASONS 9. POINT No.1 and 2 : Both these points are connected each other and in order to avoid the repetition of the facts and appreciation of the evidence, Both points are taken up together for common consideration.
10.

It is the specific case of the prosecution that, the marriage of the complainant was took place along with the accused on 12.02.2018 at temple near Chennapattana and they have registered their marriage at SubRegister office.
After the marriage, the accused and complainant were residing at No.4, 9th Cross, Hoysala Nagar, Sunkadakatte, Bangalore.

On 03.08.2021 at about 10.00 pm the accused picked up quarrel with the complainant for no reason and abused her in filthy language by The State By Kamakshipalya vs Ajit on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141882436/
4 demanding to bring the additional dowry.
The accused assaulted the complainant violently with his hands, kicked him with his legs and gave physical and mental torture to her.
Due to this, on 04.08.2021 at about 8.45 am the complainant left the house of the accused and went to Maddur and took shelter in CW7's house.
Therefore, the complainant gave complaint against accused.
11. The prosecution in order to bring home the guilt of the accused, it got examined only one witness as PW1.
Along with the oral evidence, the prosecution has produced and got marked two documents as per Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 which includes the complaint and spot mahazar.
12. Now it is necessary to analise the oral evidence of victim who is the PW1.
The said witness in her examination in chief deposed that, the accused is her husband.
CW4 is her brother.

The marriage of the accused was took place along with her at temple near Chennapattana and after the marriage when she was living in her matrimonial house alongwith the accused, there was difference of opinion for silly reasons and except the said difference of opinion, the accused did not give any physical and mental cruelty to her and did not forced to bring dowry.

The witness further deposed that, since there was difference of opinion and when she went to police station, the police had obtained her signatures on two documents, but she is not aware about the contents of said documents.

The prosecution treated this witness as hostile witness and cross examined by suggesting about the entire case of the prosecution, but the witness has denied the said suggestion put by the prosecution and further deposed that, she compromised the case alongwith the accused by obtaining the divorce.
The prosecution only got examined the victim and it has not examined any other witnesses.
13. The case of the prosecution entirely stands on the evidence of victim who is PW1.

As it is discussed above, the PW1 who is the victim herself turned hostile by deposing that, there was only difference of opinion between herself and accused and the accused never caused any incident as alleged by her in the complaint.
When the victim herself turned hostile to the case of the prosecution, there is no evidence to the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused.

Moreover,
on perusal of the oral evidence of PW1, it reveals that she has compromised the matter along with the accused.

In view of the nonsupporting of the main and material witness, this Court is of the considered view that, prosecution has miserably failed to prove the guilt of the accused for the alleged offence beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, for the said reasons this court answers point No.1and 2 in the Negative.
14. POINT No.3:

In view of discussion held on above points, this court proceeds to pass the following:
:: ORDER :: Acting u/s 248 (1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable u/s 498(A) of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act.
The bail bond of the accused and surety shall stand cancelled.
(Dictated to the stenographer transcribed by her, revised and corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 20th January, 2023) (Sandesh Prabhu B.)
